title: EqGPT infers a previously unreported equation for steepening surface gravity waves
summary: A knowledge-guided generative model trained on mathematical handbook equations generated candidate PDEs, then evaluated and optimized them against data. In a real-data case study of strongly nonlinear surface gravity waves approaching breaking, the authors report an equation not previously reported for that process.
ai_technology: EqGPT, a generative transformer using equation tokenization and a generation–evaluation–optimization loop
organization: China University of Petroleum (East China); Imperial College London; Southern University of Science and Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; University of Oxford

evidence.tested: A knowledge-guided generative model trained on mathematical handbook equations generated candidate PDEs, then evaluated and optimized them against data.
evidence.unknown: The claimed new governing equation is an inference from a particular real-world laboratory dataset and remains a model-derived description, not a universally established law. Authors used human fluid-mechanics analysis; this was one new equation result within a methods paper that also rediscovers known PDEs.
evidence.ai_role: The model proposed free-form PDE candidates using structures learned from 221 handbook equations; data-driven fit evaluation selected a candidate for the breaking-wave dataset, after which researchers analyzed its physical interpretation.
